title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying a 'loop equation' in GL2 over F_ell-algebras, i.e. over Z[1/2]-algebras with F_ell coefficients, with values in an arbitrary base Gamma. In the twisted form (9) it reads [alpha,rho] = eps [beta,sigma] eps_1(mu). Here rho and sigma are fixed matrices, eps is a scalar with eps^2 = 1 (the important case is eps = -1), and eps_1(mu) is presumably diag(mu,1). The solutions (alpha, beta, mu, eps) form a scheme G*_{rho,sigma}. The key result (10), stated on the previous page, is an isomorphism B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma -> G*_{rho,sigma}, (u,a,b) |-> (alpha = u a^{-1}, beta = u b^{-1}, mu = det u, eps = eps(b)). The factors are: B'_0, a Borel-type subgroup; T_rho, the centralizer torus of rho; and N'_sigma, the subgroup of the normalizer of sigma defined by b sigma b^{-1} = eps(b) sigma (relation (11)).

This page: (i) The map (10) lands in G*_{rho,sigma} for formal reasons. This uses only the definition of N'_sigma and an earlier identity (2), with no hypothesis on Tr sigma. (ii) Surjectivity onto all eps (locally), or just reaching eps = -1 when 2 is invertible, requires some b with b sigma b^{-1} = -sigma. Taking traces gives Tr sigma = -Tr sigma, so Tr sigma = 0 is necessary. Conversely, if Tr sigma = 0 and sigma is regular semisimple, the Weyl element of the torus T_sigma swaps the eigenvalues lambda and -lambda and does the job. So N'_sigma is an extension of mu_2 by T_sigma. (iii) G*_{rho,sigma} is made into a group scheme by transporting the product group structure from B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma. (iv) A subgroup G*(0) is singled out, corresponding to T'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma. Here T_0 = B'_0 ∩ B'_1 is the distinguished maximal torus of B'_0, written as {diag(mu,1) | mu in G_m}. (v) The subgroup G_{rho,sigma} ∩ G*(0) corresponds to T'_0 x T_rho x T_sigma, i.e. the eps = 1 part. The next page then writes G* as the semidirect product G*(0)·Lambda_0, with Lambda_0 the unipotent part L_0 of B'_0. Overall purpose: describe the solution scheme of the twisted loop equation as an explicit solvable group scheme (torus x torus x normalizer-of-torus, extended by a unipotent part), as a step toward understanding solutions of the loop equation in GL2.
errors: Notational inconsistency: (13)-(14) define T_0, but (12) and (15) use T'_0. Presumably T'_0 is T_0 viewed inside B'_0 (or a primed variant); this is harmless.
'Any eps' should be read as eps in mu_2. The trace argument only allows eps = ±1 when Tr sigma = 0 and sigma is invertible, and the next page indeed imposes eps^2 = 1.
The converse (Tr sigma = 0 suffices) tacitly needs sigma regular semisimple, i.e. det sigma invertible and discriminant invertible, together with 2 invertible.

ideas.what: Parametrization of the solution scheme of a twisted commutator equation [alpha,rho] = eps[beta,sigma]eps_1(mu) in GL2 by B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma, and transport of group structure to it
ideas.modern_name: Explicit description of a fiber of the commutator / word map in GL2 as a torsor under a solvable group scheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: No specific attribution; this is in the general area of word maps / commutator equations in SL2 (e.g. trace identities)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' following La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Existence of b normalizing sigma with b sigma b^{-1} = -sigma iff Tr sigma = 0 (2 invertible)
ideas.modern_name: Weyl group element of the centralizer torus acting by eigenvalue swap; trace-zero criterion

ideas.what: Distinguished torus T_0 = B'_0 ∩ B'_1 = {diag(mu,1)} and semidirect decomposition G* = G*(0)·Lambda_0
ideas.modern_name: Levi decomposition of a solvable group scheme

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine technical step: checking that a parametrization lands in the right scheme, a trace-zero criterion for an anti-commuting normalizer element, and transport of group structure. It is interesting only as part of the unpublished 'équation des lacets' programme, and contains no standalone new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'G_{rho,\hat sigma}' is most likely G^*_{rho,sigma}; the mark above is a star, not a hat.
In (12), the superscript on G looks like a crossed-out star followed by '*'. It may be intended as G^{**}(0), consistent with the next page mentioning both G* and G**. The image is ambiguous.

In (15), the superscript on the left-hand side is a crossed-out symbol and the right-hand intersection reads G_{rho,sigma} ∩ G^{**}_{rho,sigma}(0). The left-hand side is probably G^{*}_{rho,sigma}(0) (or a corrected variant), not G^natural.
Line 2: 'est trivial par définition de N'_σ et vu le fait noté plus haut (2)' is correct; a closing ')' is missing in the original after '(2)' (Grothendieck uses dashes).
